utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.4 in the matter of Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seselj, can you hear my words translated into Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome to you and everyone in around the courtroom. As we have not met before, let me present myself. I am Stefan Trechsel and I have been appointed by this Chamber to preside over this trial. For the record, Mr. Seselj, would you please identify yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Dr. Vojislav Seselj, university professor, and the chief enemy of The Hague Tribunal -- the chief and the main enemy of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Before going further, Mr. Seselj, as there is always news about your health up and down, let me ask you whether you feel fit to stand this appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trechsel, first of all there is no reason for you to be concerned because the operation that the Western intelligence services have resorted to, in order to gradually kill me, is proceeding successfully and my health condition is worse and worse with every day, but I am in a position to sit in the courtroom today. But I want to draw your attention to the fact that you better schedule a trial as soon as possible because I might die before it's completed, before the American, French, and British intelligence services manage to achieve their ultimate goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I take cognizance of what you are saying and you can be assured that the Chamber is determined to proceed as speedily as possible with this case. Mr. Seselj, as you certainly know, you have under the statute and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal the right to remain silent at all times during these proceedings. Am I right that I assume you will not avail yourself of the right to remain silent?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, Mr. Trechsel, that you are perfectly well informed that in my case remaining silent is out of the question. Remaining silent is insufferable for me, in life and especially in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I am aware of that. I asked you because it is in the Rules that I must recall this. I shall now explain to you the purpose of this hearing and the proceedings to which it belongs. On 29 March 2012, the Trial Chamber issued a decision amending the Order in Lieu of Indictment in this case to include your failure to comply with an order of 3 November 2011, which required you to remove a confidential submission from your website by 15 November. On 5 April 2012, you received the Serbian version of this decision. On the 29th March, the Trial Chamber also ordered that a Further Appearance be held for the accused to plea in respect of the new charge. Pursuant to Rule 50, if an amended indictment includes new charges and the accused has already appeared before a Trial Chamber in accordance with Rule 62, a Further Appearance shall be held as soon as practicable to enable the accused to enter a plea on the new charge or charges. Today's hearing concerns the amended charge of contempt in the Order in Lieu of Indictment. Specifically it concerns your failure to comply with the order of 3rd November 2011. I recall that the Order in Lieu of Indictment was originally issued on 9 May 2011, charging you with contempt of the Tribunal pursuant to Rule 77 for failing to comply with orders to remove from your web site three books and confidential submissions which contain information pertaining to protected witnesses. At the Initial Appearance on 6th July 2011, you pleaded not guilty to this charge. On 21st October 2011, the Trial Chamber amended the Order in Lieu of Indictment to include your failure to comply with an order of 15 July 2011, to remove a fourth book from the web site because it also contains confidential information. A Further Appearance on November 11 2011, the Trial Chamber entered a plea of not guilty on your behalf. Now, Mr. Seselj, have you read and understood the contents of the amended Order in Lieu of Indictment issued on 29 March 2011?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trechsel, I believe it is your duty to read out that order in its entirety and then I would say whether I understood it and whether I feel guilty or not. To be quite frank, I received the order in good time, but I was too lazy to read it. I had other things to do and other things to read. I just didn't have time for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, you know the proceedings very well. You're really conversant with them and used to them. And of course you do, in fact, have the right to have the indictment read out. And I will invite the Registrar, please, to read out the public version of the Order in Lieu of Indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Order in Lieu of Indictment. Vojislav Seselj, born in 1954, in Sarajevo, Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and currently on trial before the Tribunal, is charged with one count of contempt of the Tribunal pursuant to Rule 77(A) and 77(A)(ii) of the Rules as detailed below. Factual allegations. Vojislav Seselj is responsible for a web site, www.vseselj.com, on which he has published confidential information in breach of Chamber orders to remove the information. The material ordered to be removed are four books written by Vojislav Seselj and six confidential filings in case IT-03-67-T and IT-03-67-R77.2-A, all of which reveal confidential information about a number of protected witnesses. Vojislav Seselj has acknowledged receipt of orders which require him to remove the books and confidential filings. As of dates set in the orders, the books and the confidential filings remained publicly available on the web site. Charges. By his acts and omissions, Vojislav Seselj comitted contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rules 77(A) and 77(A)(ii) of the Rules, for knowingly and wilfully interfering with administration of justice by failing to remove from the web site confidential information in violation of orders of a Chamber. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Seselj, have you understood this Order in Lieu of Indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I understood it ambiguously or in two ways. I understood the text of the order because it was written in clear language. But I also understood that since the beginning of the endeavours of the Roman Catholic Inquisition and the establishment of Index Librorum Prohibitorum, the notorious list of forbidden books by the Roman Catholic church, it never happened that an author was held criminally responsible for a larger number of books, and I am proud of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, let me, as it is my duty by virtue of Article 62(A)(ii), to satisfy myself that you have correctly understood the indictment. Let me explain that this indictment only concerns your refusal to obey the order to remove these books from the -- from your web site. It does not, in fact, concern the contents. And the original order, you could have - and you have, maybe - appealed against those orders, but now those orders are in force. And all this trial is concerned with is your disobedience. I think it is as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Trechsel, we understand each other perfectly well. The ICTY demands from me that I destroy my books. They asked Giordano Bruno, and Galileo Galilei once upon a time to renounce their theories. Bruno refused and was burned at the stake. And Galileo, to save his life, renounced his theories and learning. I am not prepared to distance myself from my books, and if I am not prepared to do that, then I am not prepared to destroy them either. Removing them from the web site would mean their destruction, at least in one form of their appearance in public, and I am not going to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We are not dealing with this right now. Technical these are formal proceedings and that may come up at another stage. If one reads the transcript, one gets the feeling that you have said the ICTY had asked Giordano Bruno and Galileo Galilei to renounce their theories, but that, in fact, was not the ICTY. That was much earlier. But I think you are aware of that. Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trechsel, I must note that it is up to the quality of your interpreters. Since I arrived here, I have major objections to the work of your interpreters. But even the Roman Catholic Inquisition was a kind of international tribunal in its own time. It had international nature. Wherever they tried people the judges could be of different nationalities. The things that mattered was that they were convinced and faithful Catholics, and they were able to burn people at the stake. So there is no essential difference between the ICTY and the Roman Catholic Church. On the first day that I appeared here, I drew your attention to the fact that your uniforms, your robes of judges, irresistibly recall those of the Roman Catholic Inquisition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Your comparison of the Roman Catholic Church and Court with an international tribunal might be interesting. Unfortunately, this is not the situation and place where we can go on with this discussion. Mr. Seselj, are you prepared to enter a plea today, to say whether you are guilty -- you plead guilty or not, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And I ask the Registrar to enter a plea of not guilty which is now also on record. The supporting material for the Order in Lieu of Indictment has been served on you, Mr. Seselj. You have also acknowledged receipt of these papers. It is not very much indeed. The trial will be scheduled in co-ordination with other cases before this Tribunal. We will endeavour to hold it as soon as possible, and you will be given further information as to the date of pre-trial conference and the commencement of the trial. Mr. Seselj, do you already have a concept of how you plan to present your Defence, whether you want to call witnesses, how much time you need - if any - to prepare?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all I want to let you know, Mr. Trechsel, that I have four status issues to raise at this conference. So you should bear that in mind. Second, concerning the upcoming trial, I already said at the previous Status Conference or my first appearance, because this is already my third first appearance in this case, that I intend to testify myself and that I would call two to three witnesses who are conversant with the functioning of my web site. As regards my testimony, the chief -- the examination-in-chief would be conducted by my chief legal advisor, MA Dejan Mirovic, attorney at law. As for the other witnesses, I would examine them myself. Since the Prosecution is not represented here, the Trial Chamber is in charge. I suppose that it is you and your colleagues who would conduct cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That is the case. Thank you. We will probably have the opportunity to go into further detail at a pre-trial conference. This brings our hearing to an end. I thank everyone in and around the courtroom for their assistance, in particular --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I raise my fourth status issues? I have warned you that I have four issues concerning status to raise. First, I want to raise the issue of lack of jurisdiction by this Trial Chamber and this Tribunal to prosecute me in this case. This lack of jurisdiction is based primarily on the illegality of The Hague Tribunal which was founded unlawfully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Seselj, you can state these four status issues but not argue them now because they will have to be heard by the Chamber. So it's just a waste of time if you go into argument now. Just state the four points in one sentence each.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One thing is what I am going to say before the Trial Chamber at trial. However, this is a preliminary stage, and I am making an objection concerning lack of jurisdiction so that the Trial Chamber should decide on that objection before the trial. Instead of submitting it in writing I am raising it orally, because these kind of proceedings are abbreviated in nature. The entire procedure is abbreviated. It is so abbreviated that we don't even have a Prosecutor here. I just meant to state my objection as to lack of jurisdiction in two or three sentences so that you and your colleagues could decide on it before the beginning of the trial, and then once the trial begins I will go into detail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, this is a Tribunal which, although you may not acknowledge it, is very eager to conduct proceedings fairly. And this implies that it is the full Chamber which will have to hear your arguments, not just me today in this First Appearance hearing. So you may name your four objections, but please do not argue them now because it is loss of time, loss of your words.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Trechsel. You and your colleagues can also get all the information from the transcript of today's First Appearance. It is therefore not necessary, not indispensable, for your colleagues to be present; otherwise they would need to be present during my plea. Because if I had pleaded guilty, they would have had to be present here in the same moment to make a judgement. Since I did not plead guilty, I plead not guilty, I am now making an objection as to lack of jurisdiction. You, as a Trial Chamber, even if this Tribunal had been founded regularly, do not have jurisdiction to conduct these kind of proceedings against me. That is the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, you said you wanted to raise four points and you would name them. Now for the fourth or fifth time you have repeated the same challenge to the jurisdiction of this Tribunal. What are the three others ones? If you want to raise them or to mention them now, then please do so succinctly or otherwise we simply adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Then I will move to the other three challenges. The second one is actually my demand for the recusal of Judge O-Gon Kwon. That is also a preliminary issue. O-Gon Kwon is the Judge who confirmed the fourth indictment against me in January 2003. O-Gon Kwon presided over the first proceedings for contempt of court against me where I was unlawfully convicted. O-Gon Kwon presided over the second trial for contempt of court against me, where I was again unlawfully convicted. And now O-Gon Kwon appears as the president in the third trial for contempt of court in my case. And that is impossible in any civilized country in the world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: First, you go again into arguments, and I asked you just to state the objection which you can do in one sentence. Second, it is me who presides over this trial and not Judge Kwon, as I have stated in the beginning. Now your third objection, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My third objection is actually a request. In view of the fact that I have been detained for nine years and two months continuously, and in a civilized world detention is used to achieve three objectives: Firstly, to prevent the accused from fleeing; secondly, from influencing witnesses; and three, to prevent him from repeating the crime. There is no other way in which detention should restrain me from realising my elementary civic and professional rights. In Serbia on the 6th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I take it that your third request is to be released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Don't fret, Mr. Trechsel. That wouldn't be my request. My request from the Trial Chamber - and you are the only active Trial Chamber in the first instance that I am dealing with at the moment. In my main trial the Trial Chamber has completed its work and they will no longer wish to hold any Status Conferences. In the second proceedings for contempt of court, we are in the appeals stage of the proceedings. So this is the only first instance active proceedings that is currently taking place. That is why I am asking -- I am requesting from the Trial Chamber that you preside over -- in view of the fact that on the 6th of May there are elections in Serbia, that I should be allowed to hold a press conference for Serbian journalists by a videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Your request is on record. And the fourth point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say something else about this request because the nature of the request is such that I have to further explain it. I hope that you understand that I have the right to elaborate my third request. How can I expect you to decide on it if I do not sufficiently explain it. You want me to finish as soon as possible, Mr. Trechsel, but this is not smart. Please be patient and bear with me and you won't have any problems with me. You may have problems with the gist of what I am saying, but you will not have any procedural issues. Just a little patience, please. I, as a detainee, have the right to perform all of my professional duties, which will not go towards any of the three reasons for detention. My political party is appearing as a candidate in the elections. I am the first on the list for parliamentary elections, and my wife, Jadranka Seselj, is already a registered presidential candidate. We all have vested interested -- the two of us have vested interest in me appearing in public in a regular way by means of a videolink. This would be a negligible cost for The Hague Tribunal. And it is of the utmost interest for the Serbian Radical Party. I want to be given a chance to explain to the citizens of Serbia why it is important to overthrow the regime in power, and why it is even more important to prevent a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A group of traitors head by Tomislav Nikolic from taking over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You are now, Mr. Seselj, actually engaging in political speech and probably addressing people who will be watching this on the Internet in Serbia and that is not purpose of this hearing. But your demand is on record and the Trial Chamber will eventually decide on it. Your fourth point. What was your fourth point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I demand that you decide on this issue well in time in order to put in place the conditions for organising a videolink and a press conference by means of that videolink. And the fourth issue that I wish to raise is an objection. In these proceedings, again my elementary rights are being violated and that right is the right to expeditious trial. You, yourself, mentioned that the Order in Lieu of Indictment was issued on the 9th of May, 2011. Why wasn't the trial completed before the 9th of June, 2011? It has been prolonged and you have been waiting for something new to appear. If you go on procrastinating like that, the trial will never happen because there will always be something new that will crop up. Imagine a situation where you arrest somebody who comitted a real crime, and then you procrastinate, you hesitate, you do not start the trial against him, and then you create a situation where he repeats his crime again and again and again, and it is all possible if somebody is at large. The nature of "my crimes," in quotation marks, that are ascribed to me are such that I can commit "those crimes," again in quotation marks, while I am in prison. Nobody can prevent me from doing that. Even if I were to be isolated behind 15 locks and if I were prevented any contact with the outside world, they can still not prevent me from reoffending, especially due to the fact that The Hague Tribunal is engaging in sheer nonsense. They convict me for having published a book and they order me to remove the book from the Internet site and then -- again you're losing patience, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I have to see to it that the procedure runs within its frame, and we have on record your complaint that these proceedings have lasted an undue length of time and that is all what we can do today. We have it on record and it will be for the Chamber or whoever to decide. Do you have any further points that you want to raise today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to provide an additional document for my last objection. Imagine, for example, that a Trial Chamber has convicted a person for the crime of murder - and this is my additional argument - and that person is sentenced to a prison sentence, and then in the statement of reasons it is stated that that person is duty-bound to bury the victim of that crime. Anywhere in the world such judges would be found idiots. And if people at the Hague Tribunal do that, then it is found to be appropriate. They convict me for having published a book and for putting it on my Internet site, and then they keep on convicting me yet again and again for not wanting to remove that book from the Internet site. Does that sound normal, to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I am not here to answer that question, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone. Microphone for Judge Trechsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have managed to flee in good time, Mr. Trechsel.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Further Appearance adjourned at
